objective: Validate a three-agent task where two senders hold complementary private coordinates and the receiver must combine both messages to identify one row. Then, only after passing resource and disjoint calibration gates, compare message representations with schedule and call structure fixed.
task_family: Complete Cartesian product [q] x [q] with q a power of two >= 2; hidden target uniform over q^2 rows; Sender X sees only x, Sender Y sees only y, and Receiver sees the candidate table only.

task_randomness.scheme: A random 256-bit evaluator-only task key feeds separate HMAC-SHA256 counter streams for candidate order, candidate IDs, and target selection. Bounded draws use rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias.
task_randomness.public_seed_scope: Public episode seeds select reproducible episodes only when combined with the evaluator key; the seed alone is insufficient to reconstruct candidate order or target. The theoretical task prior is ideal uniform sampling; fixed-key generated shards are deterministic pseudorandom realizations under the HMAC PRF assumption.
task_randomness.key_handling: Keep the key outside version control and model-visible context. The manifest records only a short key ID. Runner, calibration, and report must use the same key ID.
task_randomness.amendment_status: Added before any model inference or pilot data collection, after an audit found that public-seed deterministic shuffles could be enumerated by a tool-enabled receiver; generator v0.3.2 aligned shard and runner episode IDs to their seed, and v0.3.3 replaced PRNG-seeded sampling with HMAC counter streams and unbiased bounded draws.

exact_references.zero_error_bound_scope: simultaneous noiseless fixed-width binary message from each coordinate source; framing, prompts, model decoding, and setup excluded

role_views.sender_x: q and the hidden target's x-coordinate only
role_views.sender_y: q and the hidden target's y-coordinate only

terminal_submission.count_as: model inference call and scored answer; not an inter-agent transmission

primary_outcomes: sum delivered application bytes for both messages
all sender and receiver input/output tokens and model calls

protocol_freeze.development_selection: On the eight seed-disjoint development episodes, choose between the two frozen NL candidates by highest exact joint success; break ties by the lexicographically lowest vector of aggregate input-plus-output tokens ordered by tokenizer ID, then lowest total UTF-8 application payload bytes, then lexical protocol ID. Do not add counts from different tokenizers into a single unit. Charge all candidate development calls and inputs as optimizer setup. Do not use development results for evaluation claims.
protocol_freeze.development_selection_horizon_policy: For the default feasibility report, amortize one-time NL-template selection setup over the eight preregistered evaluation episodes and publish raw totals alongside amortized values. This horizon is specific to the pilot and is not a deployment-lifetime estimate.
protocol_freeze.vector_setup_break_even_prediction: P6: Compare setup and per-episode costs dimension by dimension without exchange rates. A finite componentwise break-even exists only if no dimension has higher candidate per-episode cost and every dimension with equal per-episode cost has zero setup cost. Positive per-episode savings in each setup-bearing dimension yield the maximum of ceil(setup_cost/saving) across dimensions. In particular, positive selector token setup plus no token saving in a shared tokenizer rules out componentwise dominance at every horizon even if channel bytes eventually cross over.
protocol_freeze.uniform_prefix_code_prediction: P7: For q=2^w and independent uniform sender coordinates, any zero-error prefix-free binary code needs expected payload of at least w bits per source; the fixed-width code attains equality. A lower measured wire total must therefore come from a changed boundary/prior/shared-state assumption or from omitted framing, not a better prefix code under the registered model.
protocol_freeze.lossy_prefix_frontier_prediction: P8: Under the independent uniform q=4 prior, deterministic one-shot senders, a shared free self-delimiting codebook, and exact-row 0-1 loss, the pure-strategy expected-payload frontier includes 3 expected payload bits at 9/16 joint success, with 4 bits worst case. This is not matched to the fixed-width 3-bit hard-cap frontier. Randomized mixtures are outside the calculation. Exhaustive finite-alphabet enumeration must agree with the partition/Huffman oracle; no practical advantage is predicted unless complete measured costs improve or transfer is shown.
protocol_freeze.parser_policy: compact_kv and strict_json require exact canonical strings; decimal_index requires a canonical zero-based base-10 integer with no leading zeros; fixed_binary requires exactly log2(q) bits; concise_nl and short_nl accept only their exact frozen canonical sentences as mechanically decidable; AutoForm is a prompt-selected open-format arm with no grammar or deterministic encoder, so format validity and message semantic fidelity are unknown unless a separately frozen evaluation is added.
protocol_freeze.amendment_status: Before any v0.3 model inference or pilot data collection, added the decimal-index shorthand control after auditing earlier model outputs that spontaneously used decimal-only messages, a second frozen English template with an eight-episode seed-disjoint selector, and a separate prompt-selected AutoForm-style open-format arm based on the official paper/source audit. AutoForm is not presented as a fixed language; syntax/fidelity are not mechanically scored. These amendments add no inference evidence.
protocol_freeze.execution_gate: No inference until model IDs, tokenizer IDs, endpoint settings, resource preflight, evaluator task key, and disjoint perfect full-information ledger are supplied and validated.

natural_language_baseline: The eight-episode development selection among concise_nl and short_nl is a small frozen-template optimization, not an open-ended prompt search. The selected prompt is identified only by development data and must be evaluated on the disjoint evaluation shard. Charge every development candidate's full sender and receiver calls, input/output tokens, and channel bytes to optimizer setup. The separate AutoForm arm asks models to choose a concise non-natural-language medium at runtime and is scored by exact end-task success; its free-form messages have no fixed parser. The decimal_index arm is a task-specific numeric shorthand, not natural language. This study is not a reproduction of AutoForm's HotpotQA benchmark and does not establish superiority over trained selectors such as OPTiMACS.
fixed_code_semantics: For q=2^w, encode each coordinate index as exactly w bits in its sender slot. The fixed schedule identifies which slot is x or y. Count protocol instructions and codebook exposition in model input tokens; measure delivered payload and envelope bytes separately.
analysis: Pair all representation arms by episode_id and keep all preregistered held-out episodes. Report exact task-level discordances and descriptive uncertainty only for this pilot. Do not use development or capability-calibration outcomes to filter evaluation tasks. Treat all twenty-one pairwise representation contrasts among the seven registered arms as one exploratory family and correct or explicitly label unadjusted p-values. For the prompt-selected AutoForm arm, report syntax validity and semantic fidelity as unmeasured rather than invalid; score exact receiver task success and all costs. Plot success against both delivered channel bytes and complete inference tokens; do not combine unlike tokenizers or collapse the two budgets into one score.
capability_gate: Before any comparison call, the Receiver must answer every disjoint calibration episode correctly when supplied both exact coordinates. Calibration tasks must not occur in the evaluation shard.
resource_gate: Before any local model load or request, satisfy the repository's current same-host CPU/GPU/memory/port preflight, request timeout, hard call cap, and automatic-stop requirements. Each batch is limited to 12 planned model requests. A failed preflight stops before artifacts are loaded or endpoints contacted.
batching: Both-source representation conditions use at most four evaluation episodes per batch (4 x 3 calls = 12). Single-source conditions use at most six episodes per batch (6 x 2 calls = 12). No-message and full-information batches use at most 12 episodes. Every condition uses the same task manifest, evaluation IDs, models, endpoint settings, and decoding parameters where applicable.
prediction: If both source messages are required and the receiver is capability-qualified, full-inference success should exceed either one-source arm. Any representation ranking may vary with q and should be assessed after charging both source calls and receiver decoding. Fixed-width binary minimizes ideal payload bits but may lose after prompt, decoding, and model-error costs.
claim_limits: This deterministic Cartesian task is a calibration family, not a naturalistic collaboration benchmark.
The oracle bound does not predict LLM token efficiency or model success.
A single-q pilot cannot establish a scaling law or generalized language advantage.
Prompts and deterministic parsers are frozen, but endpoint/model settings remain pending; no inference has been run or is authorized by this preregistration alone.
The keyed task generator protects against reconstruction from public seeds only; it does not protect raw evaluator ledgers if those ledgers or the key are exposed.
expected_runtime: Pure Python standard library; task generation and analytic controls make no model or network calls.
